title: Scheduled work-head position equality
statement: Let $M$ be a binary multi-tape Turing machine with $k$ work tapes, let $m,s,t\in\mathbb{N}$, and let $\tau$ be a work-tape index. For the movement-count row at time $s$ on the all-zero input of length $m$, and two target words both taken from the movement counts at time $t$, the comparison flag at the positive and negative slots for $\tau$ is true exactly when the work-head positions at times $s$ and $t$ on tape $\tau$ are equal.
replaced: For every oblivious machine, reference length $m$, times $s$ and $t$, and work tape $\tau$, the comparison flag of the stored row at time $s$ against the target counts at time $t$, taken at the positive and negative slots of $\tau$, is true exactly when the public work-head position on $\tau$ at time $s$ equals the position at time $t$.
